swe.problem_statement:
Broken pi
pi has limited precision in AcbField (but not in ArbField)

```
julia> pi
π = 3.1415926535897...

julia> typeof(pi)
Irrational{:π}

julia> AcbField(100)(pi)
[3.14159265358979323846264338328 +/- 3.83e-30]

julia> sin(AcbField(100)(pi)) # good
[+/- 3.33e-30]

julia> sin(AcbField(200)(pi)) # good
[+/- 2.61e-60]

julia> sin(AcbField(300)(pi)) # ???
[1.096917440979352e-77 +/- 2.69e-93]

julia> sin(AcbField(400)(pi)) # ???
[1.096917440979352076742130626395698021050758237e-77 +/- 6.43e-123]

julia> sin(AcbField(400)(BigFloat(pi,400))) # good
[6e-122 +/- 4.63e-123]

julia> sin(ArbField(400)(pi)) # good
[+/- 8.40e-121]
```

swe.interface:
Method: RealField(::Irrational, prec::Int) → RealFieldElem
Location: src/arb/Real.jl – overload of the RealField call operator
Inputs: an Irrational constant (e.g., `MathConstants.pi`, `MathConstants.e`, `MathConstants.catalan`, `MathConstants.eulergamma`) and a precision integer `prec`.
Outputs: a `RealFieldElem` representing the constant at the requested precision. Internally calls `_arb_set` to set the value; raises an error only for unsupported Irrationals.
Description: Constructs a real field element from a known mathematical constant with a user‑specified precision. Used by tests via `RR(MathConstants.pi)` etc.

Function: _arb_set(x::RealFieldElemOrPtr, y::Irrational) → Nothing
Location: src/arb/Real.jl
Inputs: `x` – a real field element (or pointer) to be mutated; `y` – an Irrational constant.
Outputs: none (mutates `x`). Calls the three‑argument version with the default field precision.
Description: Convenience wrapper that sets a real field element to a constant using the field’s default precision.

Function: _arb_set(x::RealFieldElemOrPtr, y::Irrational, p::Int) → Nothing
Location: src/arb/Real.jl
Inputs: `x` – a real field element (or pointer); `y` – an Irrational constant; `p` – target precision in bits.
Outputs: none (mutates `x`). Dispatches to the appropriate libflint constant constructor (`arb_const_pi`, `arb_const_e`, `arb_const_catalan`, `arb_const_euler`) or falls back to converting via `BigFloat` for other Irrationals.
Description: Low‑level routine that writes a supported constant into a real field element at a given precision.

Method: ArbField(::Irrational) → ArbFieldElem
Location: src/arb/arb.jl – overload of the ArbField call operator
Inputs: an Irrational constant.
Outputs: an `ArbFieldElem` representing the constant at the field’s default precision. Internally creates a fresh element and invokes `_arb_set`.
Description: Constructs an arbitrary‑precision real field element from a mathematical constant without an explicit precision argument. Used by tests via `RR(MathConstants.pi)` when `RR` is an `ArbField`.

Function: _arb_set(x::ArbFieldElemOrPtr, y::Irrational) → Nothing
Location: src/arb/arb.jl
Inputs: `x` – an arb field element (or pointer); `y` – an Irrational constant.
Outputs: none (mutates `x`). Calls the three‑argument version with the parent field’s default precision.
Description: Convenience wrapper for setting an arb field element to a constant using the field’s default precision.

Function: _arb_set(x::ArbFieldElemOrPtr, y::Irrational, p::Int) → Nothing
Location: src/arb/arb.jl
Inputs: `x` – an arb field element (or pointer); `y` – an Irrational constant; `p` – desired precision in bits.
Outputs: none (mutates `x`). Handles `pi`, `MathConstants.e`, `MathConstants.catalan`, and `MathConstants.eulergamma` via libflint constant constructors; otherwise falls back to `BigFloat` conversion.
Description: Low‑level routine that writes a supported constant into an arb field element at a specified precision.

llm_metadata.reasoning: The issue reports incorrect precision for π in AcbField and expects sin(π) to be zero at high precision, providing reproducible REPL examples. The added tests check that π and other mathematical constants are correctly represented and that functions like sin and log produce near‑exact results at 400 bits, matching the intended fix. No test‑suite coupling, naming, external URLs, or unrelated patches are detected, and the tests directly validate the behavior described, so the task is clearly solvable. Therefore the classification is A (solvable).

review.summary: Nemo.jl silently lost precision when constructing ball-arithmetic elements from Julia Irrational constants: conversion fell through to the generic `_arb_set(x, y::Real, p)` path, which built `BigFloat(y)` at the ambient (default 256-bit) precision and only then rounded up to the requested precision. Issue #2099 documents the concrete symptom: `sin(AcbField(300)(pi))` returns a bogus nonzero value around 1.09e-77 instead of a ball containing zero, while `sin(AcbField(400)(BigFloat(pi,400)))` and `sin(ArbField(400)(pi))` are correct. The fix adds `_arb_set` methods for `Irrational` in both src/arb/arb.jl and src/arb/Real.jl that dispatch to the FLINT constant routines (arb_const_pi/e/catalan/euler) at the target precision, and rewrites the `(r::ArbField)(x::Irrational)` / `(r::RealField)(x::Irrational, prec)` constructors to route through that helper. Because the Acb/Complex constructors set their real part via `_arb_set`, the fix propagates to the complex types that were the visible failure in the issue.
review.evidence: Issue #2099 ("Broken pi") gives a reproducible numeric wrong-answer at precisions above the BigFloat default, with a correct-vs-incorrect comparison in the same session. PR #2104 explicitly states "Resolves #2099" and notes tests were added, matching the test files touched (test/arb/arb-test.jl, Real-test.jl, acb-test.jl, Complex-test.jl). Runtime evidence reports a stable differential over 3 repetitions with the full suite passing after the fix. Minimization kept 4 of 6 hunks and reports all kept hunks necessary and globally minimal; the two dropped hunks are a pure de-duplication of `_arb_set(x, y::BigFloat, p)` in each file. The change is confined to conversion helpers plus the parent-object call overloads for `Irrational`, mirrored across the arb and Real implementations.
review.missing_evidence: No explicit trigger test names are recorded (trigger_tests is empty), so the exact failing assertion in the pre-fix state is not visible. The Complex.jl/acb.jl code path that consumes `_arb_set` is not included in the diff, so the propagation to the complex types is inferred rather than directly verified. PR title/body for the commit itself are empty; traceability is PR-mediated through issue #2104.
review.validation_risks: The rewritten `else` branch replaces the previous `error("constant not supported")` with a BigFloat fallback, so previously-throwing inputs (e.g. MathConstants.golden) now succeed. If a pre-existing test asserted that error, the fix would be a behavior extension rather than a pure fix; nothing in the provided evidence indicates such a test. The two files diverge slightly: Real.jl uses `precision(Balls)` for the no-precision method while arb.jl uses `precision(parent(x))`, which may behave differently when `x` is a raw pointer. Assertions on interval midpoints/radii for irrational constants can be brittle across FLINT versions, so tests should check containment rather than exact digit strings.
review.suggested_tests: Assert containment/precision rather than exact output: for p in (100, 200, 300, 400, 1000), check `contains_zero(sin(AcbField(p)(pi)))` and `contains_zero(sin(ArbField(p)(pi)))`, and that the radius scales with p (roughly 2^-p) instead of saturating near 2^-256. Compare `ArbField(p)(pi)` against `const_pi(ArbField(p))` and `RealField()(pi, p)` against `const_pi(RealField(), p)` for equality/overlap. Repeat for MathConstants.e, catalan, and eulergamma, and add the same checks on ComplexField/AcbField constructors. Include a regression case at p=300 (the precision where the issue first misbehaved) and one case for a non-special Irrational to pin the BigFloat fallback precision.
